claims.text: Selective surface segregation of Cu governs the initiation and progression of the phase transition in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu is the lowest-melting element in FeNiCrCoCu.
Surface-segregated Cu forms a premelted, liquid-like layer.
The Cu-rich premelted layer nucleates and propagates bulk melting.
The starting nanoparticles are homogeneous and solid, with uniformly distributed elements and minimal surface segregation.
A pre-thermal treatment or altered ambient chemistry can promote surface Cu segregation.
Chemical passivation can suppress surface Cu segregation or Cu migration.
Using an inert atmosphere eliminates oxidation during the heating experiment.
A Cu-enriched surface layer undergoes a liquid-like transition before the remainder of the nanoparticle.
The Cu-rich premelted layer alters the local energy landscape and lowers the barrier for further phase transformation.
At elevated temperatures, Cu preferentially migrates to the nanoparticle surface because of its lower melting point.
Nanoparticles with enhanced surface Cu segregation will have a lower melting-onset temperature than nanoparticles with suppressed segregation.
Nanoparticles with enhanced surface Cu segregation will melt from the surface inward.
Nanoparticles with suppressed Cu segregation will exhibit a higher and more spatially uniform melting onset.
Nanoparticle size and heating rate may modify the observed melting behavior.
Trace impurities may influence thermally induced phase behavior.
A statistically significant failure of the Cu-enriched set to show both a lower melting onset and surface-initiated melting relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
